Vabalninkas Jewish Сemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Panevėžio apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Vabalninkas was the birthplace of Rabbi Elazar Menachem Man Shach (1899–2001), the leading Lithuanian-Jewish Orthodox rabbi in Bnei Brak and founder of the Degel HaTorah political party, which continues to represent non-Hasidic Ashkenazi Jews in the Israeli Knesset today — one of the most influential rabbis of the 20th-century Orthodox world. During a July 1915 pogrom staged by retreating Cossacks, the town was set on fire along with its communal record books, though residents managed to save the Torah scrolls and carry them into exile; after the war, the community rebuilt two synagogues that still stand today, nicknamed 'Die Kalte Shul' (the Cold Synagogue, used in summer) and 'Die Wareme Shul' (the Warm Synagogue, used in winter). On August 26, 1941, Vabalninkas's Jews were transferred to Pasvalys, documented elsewhere in this collection, and taken with that town's own Jews to the Zadeikiai forest, where 1,349 people were shot and buried in prepared pits.
